title: Shard-conscious TTL+LRU arbitration with atomic reclamation guarantees
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: As we scale continuous batching across heterogeneous GPU pools and introduce per-prefix KV affinity, simple global LRU or pure TTL policies cause either: (1) prefix starvation where popular prefixes displace important long-tail prefixes; (2) transient correctness windows where requests observe missing KV state due to non-atomic reclamation; or (3) suboptimal GPU memory fragmentation leading to higher OOM and degraded latency.

Goal: Design and implement a shard-conscious arbitration layer that combines TTL and LRU signals, enforces per-prefix soft quotas, and provides atomic reclamation semantics so that in-flight batches never observe a partial prefix state. The system must be memory-efficient on GPU, support fast path for hot prefixes, and include formal invariants and tests for correctness.

Proposed approach summary: 
- Maintain per-shard per-prefix metadata (last_access_ts, ttl_expiry, size_bytes, hot_score) in a compact metadata slab on host memory with an optional pinned mapping for GPUs requiring low-latency checks.
- Arbitration rule: candidates for reclamation are scored by a composite priority = alpha * age_rank + beta * ttl_proximity + gamma * prefix_penalty, where prefix_penalty implements a soft quota to protect prefixes with recent high hit-rate. We will tune alpha/beta/gamma using offline traces.
- Atomic reclamation protocol: use a two-phase marker update per prefix: (1) mark-for-reclaim set (atomically flip a one-bit tombstone and publish an incremented epoch), (2) safe-retire once outstanding batch fence counters per shard reach epoch. This ensures no batch sees partially reclaimed KV entries.
- Shard-aware compaction: when reclaiming, prefer coalescing free blocks to reduce fragmentation; track extent sizes and prefer evicting small extents first on GPUs with limited allocator granularity.
- Fallbacks: when memory pressure is critical, allow emergency TTL-ignore evictions with a conservative circuit-breaker and telemetry alerts.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Unit/integration tests proving that in-flight batch reads against a prefix never observe missing keys while eviction is progressing (fuzzer that injects concurrent reads/writes and asserts monotonic visibility).
- End-to-end benchmark showing <=5% P99 latency regression under synthetic load compared to baseline and >=20% reduction in OOMs on mixed workloads.
- Telemetry: new metrics for prefix_hot_score, reclaim_epoch_lag, fragmentation_ratio, and emergency_eviction_count.
- Rollout plan: staged rollout to dedicated clusters then hosted canaries.

Notes on trade-offs: 
- We accept slightly higher metadata overhead in host memory (+~5-8MB per 1M prefixes) to achieve atomic reclamation guarantees.
- Exact tuning of alpha/beta/gamma will be data-driven; initial conservative defaults favor TTL when expiry is imminent to reclaim stale long-lived prefixes.

Safety & rollback: feature gate behind runtime-1.24 flag; can disable arbitration and fall back to current LRU+TTL hybrid. Add a fast kill switch to bypass marker protocol and revert to immediate evictions in emergency with documented risk of transient missing-key observations.
design_notes: Detailed design doc: drive.redwood.internal/runtime/kv/shard-arb-v1 (private). Key invariants: (I1) monotonic visibility: once a key is observed present at epoch E, later reads at epoch >= E should not observe missing unless a committed retire has advanced; (I2) reclaim atomicity: a prefix retires only after all shards report epoch fence >= marker_epoch; (I3) memory safety: allocator never frees extent referenced by active KV handles. We plan to formalize I1 and I2 in the unit test harness and stress-fuzz for I3.
implementation_plan: 1) metadata slab and API (2 wks) 2) marker epoch + fence counters (1 wk) 3) arbitration scorer + offline tuning (1 wk) 4) GPU compaction hooks + allocator integration (2 wks) 5) tests and fuzzers (2 wks) 6) telemetry, dashboards, and canary rollout (1 wk)
test_plan: concurrency-fuzzer: 10k runs across combinations of batch sizes and interleavings
perf: bench mixed prefix popularity traces vs baseline
